A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. All appendix pages are unchanged, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model experiments on algorithmic reasoning, DNF counting, and graph-coloring sampling in Section 5 and Appendix D, including accuracy and distributional results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Tables 2–3 and Figures 6–7 and 10–11. Results retained from v2 remain original empirical results of the work.

M1.justification: The CoT, Coconut, and looped-Transformer procedures are unchanged. Section 4.1 now explicitly emphasizes stochastic output decoding, which v2 already allowed and Appendix C.1 already formalized; this does not introduce stochastic latent computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate finite-group word problems, graph connectivity, arithmetic evaluation, edit distance, DNF counting, and graph-coloring sampling. Appendix D retains the same data-generation scenarios and task requirements.

E2.justification: The evaluated CoT and looped-Transformer comparisons are unchanged, including CoT training through uniform trajectory selection and stepwise internalization. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Experimental configurations, training schedules, sample sizes, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Figure 7's revised caption identifies sampling error as TV distance, already specified by v2's axis label and Appendix D.2.2; this is a caption correction, not a changed metric.

E4.justification: Both retain the loop-count/input-size analysis in Figure 6, trajectory-shortening analyses in Table 3 and Figure 10, and coloring-distribution analyses in Figures 7 and 11. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: The independent-sampling procedures, fixed graph-seed disclosure, and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and Figures 6–7 and 10–11 retain identical numerical results, curves, and output distributions. The new Figure 7 discussion describes the existing histogram rather than reporting an additional empirical outcome.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, separation results, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–C are unchanged. The clearer statement about stochastic latent-model outputs restates the existing formal model.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the parallel-computation and randomized-counting claims. Section 6 adds broader practical guidance that latent reasoning suits efficiently solvable problems whereas CoT is more effective for more complex problems.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces iteration-budget discussion and general support for separation with an explicit interpretation of Figure 7 as better uniform solution coverage by CoT and concentration by looped TF. Section 6 also broadens applicability guidance; the downstream-task caveat remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-repository link in the abstract. Appendix D's implementation, training, and inference details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish an added access pointer, without establishing the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the precise account of padded looped Transformers matching uniform TC^k with a broader statement connecting parallel reasoning to Coconut and diffusion models, citing already-listed works. Table 1 and cited-work membership remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the introduction, related work, probabilistic-model explanation, results discussion, and conclusion. Section ordering and appendix structure remain intact. The front-page preprint notice becomes an ICML proceedings notice, with additional small terminology and capitalization edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes 'Sequentially' to 'Sequentiality'; captions for Figures 1, 4, and 7 are revised, including the sampling-metric correction. Text reflows locally, but all figures and tables are retained without changes to the plotted results.

improvement.justification: The corrected Figure 7 caption, clearer stochastic-output explanation, and new code pointer improve documentation. However, Section 6's efficient-versus-complex recommendation extends beyond the unchanged conditional separations, while Section 2.2 loses a precise prior-work comparison. These documentation gains and losses in scientific precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
